units.function: Cross-surface contract tests for parsing and presenting Gemini CLI v0.38 stream-json events, structured questions, session failure and turn-limit results.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> @paperclipai/adapter-gemini-local server/UI/CLI exports; no Paperclip database/service, Gemini process, credential, network or real model is exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Vendor JSONL system/message/result/error event, opaque session/model, assistant summary/question, token usage/USD cost, error text, stop reason/exit code and normalized UI/CLI event.
units.lifecycle: Parse vendor stream lines -> extract adapter-local continuation/usage/result/question/error -> classify retry/fresh-session signals -> render normalized UI or CLI output.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 8/8 hermetically. It pins a useful v0.38 compatibility slice but omits malformed/evolving streams, output redaction/bounds, cancellation/backpressure and most failure disagreements.
units.designRationale: Centralize known Gemini wire-shape handling, use structured stop signals rather than error-text guesses for turn limits and keep server/UI/CLI interpretations aligned during a vendor CLI format change.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equal vendor Connectors that normalize progress, usage, input requests and terminal causes while keeping private sessions, vendor wording and model-specific retry quirks outside core/application contracts.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only inside a Gemini Connector package. Preserve v0.38 fixtures and structured turn-limit handling, but expose versioned ConnectorEvent/Usage/OperatorInputRequest/TerminalCause codes; keep continuation handles private, redact/bound all display/log output and add compatibility fixtures per supported CLI version.
units.responsibilityConflict: A structured vendor question is not a Company OS Approval, and the parsed session/error/summary lacks Work, responsible human, permission/data grant, evidence digest and result provenance. Raw vendor strings must never determine responsibility transitions.
units.securityFindings: HIGH raw-output risk: provider error/assistant strings flow to UI/CLI with no tested redaction, control-character or length guard. HIGH contract brittleness: unrecoverable sessions depend on English phrase matching. HIGH private-state boundary: vendor session ID is parsed alongside normalized output and must not leak into core/public events. MEDIUM compatibility gap: only selected v0.38 events are tested. MEDIUM accounting integrity: token/cost values are accepted without validity, currency or authoritative-source checks.
